description:
hi there~

I’m aperture, and I’m a teen artist and storyteller taking on the Nasa Space Apps Challenege solo this year. I’m building an immersive digital experience and turning the lonely, rusted history of equipment on the moon into something beautiful ✨🌗 Not looking for any teammates, but excited to see y’all’s work!
summary: Our project is a storytelling archive as well as an information package teaching school age and space enthusiasts about the life of the hardware on the Moon, Mars, and space. We developed a interactive digital zine with clickable hyperlinks and simple doodles to cater to a younger audience and fill them with knowledge while keeping it fun and immersive at the same time. We wanted to highlight the reality of the discarded equipment by anthropomorphising it, potraying them like fallen beings lost to space, waiting for the next generation of explorers to return and find them as well as their years of trapped data. We focused on keeping it broad while highlighting specific pieces with legendary stories such as being repurposed twice, or having a lifespan for longer than expected to create a powerful narrative that engages the viewer. This project simplifies and makes the information easy to digest, nurturing a new generation of space enthusiasts, and redefines our memory of these artifacts, this archive reminding us that the equipment is not useless anymore and still beautiful inventions for future generations to reclaim.
details:
Our project teaches young space enthusiasts about NASA's discarded equipment on the Moon, Mars, and deep space. This digital zine is interactive and utilizes simple doodles, cultivating a sense of interest in space among the younger generation. The intended impact of the project is to spread knowledge and improve outer space literacy in a easy and engaging way. I used canva to create my project so that it is minimalist and eye-catching, using clickable hyperlinks and click to appear images as well as rotating images, along with my skills in simple doodling. My project uses creative storytelling, antromorphomising the machines in the main pages of the zine and then describing the indivual facts of each piece of equipment. This makes sure the core narrative is captivating while still getting the key information to the viewer.

Some factors our team considered were how to balance young engagement with technical accuracy, ensuring every mission status, deployment, and fascinating story of the hardware is grounded in real NASA data. We also considered what design we should use for the zine, and decided to keep it to a minimalist aesthetic for the young reader's easy navigation. Lastly, we thought about our long term perspective on space sustainability. As humanity continues expanding its footprint in outer space, so did our relationship with equipment in outer space, and we spent a lot of time ensuring we sent out this message and our storytelling was aligned.
